$comment: Global economy constants from design doc §8. All first-pass values — tune in Phase 3 against pacing targets.

costGrowth.$note: almanac is the geometric step on a REPEATABLE Almanac line (see almanac.json). A repeatable line is a sink, never a gate, which is the only reason an exponential cost is safe here: its benefit is additive per level (linear) against a cost that is exponential, so it tapers forever without ever walling. Gates must scale at most linearly with the fold count — see rites.json's demandGrowth note for why.

gifts.$note: design §4: gift piles — one pile earned per verse sung (lifetime, across Migrations), one yes each. pileGoods units of the node's OWN resource (§13: you leave a pile of what the flock likes), spent from camp stock at the node the player chooses; the arrival is that resource's specialist species (derived from species.json traits — no per-event species config) and takes the node as its post. A pile is refused where the specialist already walks or no specialist exists. pileGoods is a first guess.

delivery.$note: hauling as a throughput system is retired (it raced two absolute rates - gather vs carry - whose growth lanes could never be kept level, and any tuning was wrong for either a 4- or a 6-slot kith). Goods now reach camp automatically and losslessly: each node's pickings pool up and land as one batch every batchSeconds. The cadence exists ONLY so design S5 quality rolls stay per-batch (never per unit) and a Choice find keeps landing as a discrete windfall - it is not a cap, and nothing gathered is ever lost.

kith.$note: design Â§4 ladder: a slot is the right to hold a post; companions past the slots rest at camp. One slot from minute one; one more the FIRST time each slotVerseZones verse is sung (never unsung, and carried across Migrations); the last two are store purchases (the starter bundle, then the plain slot product) â€” slotsBase + slotVerseZones + 2 purchasable must equal slotsMax, which the validator enforces. Named verses rather than a tally since 2026-08-11: the ladder counted LIFETIME verses sung across 2/5/10, which paid for folding early and often rather than for walking a trail to its end, and left the second place landing in run 2 (design Â§8's known consequence). The three are chosen early/mid/late off the zones' own minMigration gates: bramble-hedgerows is the second trail and lands mid-run-1, mistfen-marsh opens at fold 2 so its verse lands in run 3, cloudreach-peaks at fold 5 so its verse lands in run 6 (Mo's call, 2026-08-11: the last place belongs on the last trail, and highland-crags at run 5 put it one fold short of the end for no reason the player could see). Sunfield's verse is deliberately not one of them (it is the first thing anyone sings, before a place means anything), and neither is old-growth-wood's (run 1's last verse is the fold gate, so a place there would pay for finishing rather than for going deeper). Note the peaks now carry BOTH the ladder's last rung and the run's narrative capstone; if that reads as one beat too many at the same fire, the crags are where the place moves back to. generatorGatherPosts is what the Rite generator assumes a plausible kith can hold at gather nodes at once (run-2+ rites; earned and purchased slots are never assumed beyond it). gatherPerSecond is a familiar's base gather rate at its post (was an implicit 1.0) â€” cut to 0.1 on 2026-07-31 when hauling retired, because lossless deliveries roughly x4-5'd effective camp income, then raised to 0.3 on 2026-08-03: 0.1 overshot the correction and a posted familiar read as barely worth the slot. Still a first guess; absent or 0 in hand-built data means 1.0.

crafting.$note: first-guess Phase-3 number, not in design doc — seconds per craft at every station before craftSpeedMult upgrades divide it. Tune against the §2 pacing targets (first recipe cooked ~20 min).

tools.$note: flint is knapped (no forge); each later tier also consumes an ingot batch (see recipes). deepsteel is the §5 'deep ores' tier past steel — smelted from the Hollows' deep-ore seams

mastery.$note: curve and xpPerUnit are first guesses, not in the design doc — mastery XP per unit gathered at the node, rung r costs base·growth^r. yieldBonusPerLevel applies to both yield and the raw resource's sell value (§4 '+5% yield/value').

verdure.$note: renownDivisor re-anchored on observed play (2026-08-04 playtest): the model's 2800 assumed ~280K Renown at the first fold, but a real run reached ~110M by fold 1 and 1.38B by fold 2, banking hundreds of Verdure against a ~166-point tree. 1e6 restores the design targets on real numbers: ~10 at fold 1, tree done around fold 3-4, the repeatable line after. Verdure = floor((lifetimeRenown / renownDivisor) ^ exponent); exponent stays 0.5 — the sqrt shape is a design commitment (design doc section 9). Existing saves keep their banked total (it never shrinks), so an over-banked playtest save just forecasts +0 until the curve catches up.

xp.$note: gatherPerUnit tuned to 3 via the balance model (docs/economy-model.xlsx) so gathering pulls roughly even with familiar time-XP as a Renown source (§9 'every good handled credits Renown') — at 1 it was only ~22% of Renown. Note this also credits warden gathering-skill XP, but recipe gates (max level 5) are already met in minutes at any value, so progression is unaffected. craftPerBatch is still a first guess. Confirm in playtest.

offline.$note: The away ladder is rescaled to run 2 h -> 12 h (2026-08-03). It used to start at 4 h and top out unbounded: the raise-to rungs stopped at 12 h but the Store's endless +0.25 h/level and three additive pieces kept climbing past it forever. Now the run starts on a short night that has to be earned longer, and maxCapHours is the ceiling every source is measured against. The authored kit lands on exactly 12 with nothing to spare — Long Watch III (9 h) plus the Oilskin Tarp, the Old-Growth Bounty spread and the Almanac Desk at +1 h each — so the Store's per-level hours are the early accelerator and the overflow they eventually make is what the ceiling is there to catch.

quality.$note: design §5: quality rolls per delivery batch (Poor 96% / Decent ~3.5% +50% value / Choice 0.5% base). choiceValueMult is a first guess — the 'windfall' sale isn't priced in the doc. choiceChance = (choiceBaseChance + owned choiceChanceBonus effects) * (1 + tending.choiceChanceBonus while the node's tend window is live) — flat bonuses add points, Tending multiplies (§8).

amber.$note: Amber (design §10): the premium currency's free earn + soft sink. Finds roll per tick at watchers * digFindsPerHour — LINEAR and ONCE for the round, not per site and not scaled by digSpeedMult (a separate channel from field sketches — a fully-recorded map keeps surfacing amber; it's old resin with an ancient insect in it, the one thing takeable). It was per-site * digSpeedMult until 2026-08-02 and both compounded silently: six dig sites against a multiplicative watch stack (brush screens x2 * deep sight x1.5 * hollow relics x1.25 * lantern bearers x1.2 * an ashen season x1.5 * reed screens x1.5 = ~10x) reached ~7 amber/hour, so a single login's catch-up paid ~70 — roughly 30x the ~40/week lean below, against a game whose only sink is the time skip. Flat is the deliberate answer: the earn no longer grows with the map, so the number here is the whole rate and reads the way it is written. The deep amber (ambers.json) keeps both — it is lore pacing with four total payouts, and the watch stack shortening that walk is the intent; a time-skip instantly credits timeSkipHours of full live production for timeSkipCostAmber. timeSkipDailyCapHours bounds PAID skips to that many skipped hours per real day (a leaky budget refilling at cap/24 per wall hour, so it holds on every timescale, no midnight cliff; 0/absent = uncapped). At 24 it pins a heavy spender to at most x2 a free player's pace: a day holds 24 natural sim-hours and skips may add at most 24 more — sim-time is the only thing money buys here, so this one number IS the whale throttle. The rewarded-ad skip sits OUTSIDE the budget (free players get it too — it's part of the baseline both sides share). adDripAmber is the small pile a rewarded ad gives; weeklyCacheAmber is the once-a-week Play Games cache (design §11). renameCostAmber is what a familiar's rename asks — the arrival naming too, unless you keep the suggested name. Raised 5 -> 30 on 2026-08-05: at 5 it was loose change beside a 15-amber time-skip and the sink did nothing, where 30 is two skips forgone, i.e. most of the ~40/week-free lean, so naming a companion is a real choice a free player saves for. Deliberately NOT charged for keeping the suggested arrival name, which is what keeps the price off the critical path. wardenRenameCostAmber is naming the WARDEN, at 50 — dearer than a companion's 30 because it is bought once for the body the player wears across every fold and it reads on every page, where a companion's name reads on one card. Both charge on a change only: re-typing the same name, or blank, is free. callingGiftAmber is what answering a gift pile asks alongside the pile itself (design 2026-08-06 sink slate's early-game entry) — charged only through Gifts.LeavePile, so unasked arrivals (the first vole and raven, a bonded companion crossing the fold, the Drover's pony) never pay it, and a short warden's pile waits unconsumed rather than being refused. campNameCostAmber names this run's CAMP, at 40 — between a companion's 30 and the warden's 50, and unlike either it is paid once per RUN: the name folds with the camp at Migration, which makes naming a ritual of each region and the first RECURRING expressive sink (design 2026-08-06 slate). considerationCostAmber is a consideration pressed on the drover — the Exchange's standing deal re-draws AT ONCE, never repeating the deal it replaces; the re-deal count persists per window and mixes into the offer seed so a reload cannot reroll what the bribe bought (Exchange.PressConsideration). secondQueueCostAmber buys the run's SECOND craft-queue slot — each station may then hold two standing orders (Crafting.OrderCapacity); bought per run, lapsing at the fold, which is what makes it recur as a sink. It removes craft latency, never material walls (a queue cannot mint inputs), and it stays at +1 by design. The keepsake page (a mounted journal page remembering the run) was a third expressive sink here and was REMOVED 2026-08-11: its whole payoff was one shelf line naming the camp, which reads 'an unnamed camp' unless the 40-amber camp name was bought first — and the name is snapshotted at mounting, so the two purchases only combined in one order. All first guesses against the DILIGENT lean of ~120/week (drip ~84 + dig finds ~20 + cache 20 — DECIDED 2026-08-06; the lazy player's ~40 is the floor, not the anchor).

store.$note: real-money catalogue constants. The starter bundle (Play Level Up's initial purchase offer) grants a kith slot plus this one-time pile of Amber; the plain kith_slot product grants the sixth slot alone. The amber packs (amber_pack_small/large) are consumable buy-amber products granting these piles. Amounts are first guesses (starter ~2 time-skips; small pack ~3, large ~10).

observation.$note: design §6 (observe · sketch · release). sketch rate = watchers * baseSketchesPerHour * digSpeedMult upgrades * the site's summed unrecorded rarity, rolled per tick; a field sketch is guaranteed once pityTimerHoursWatched hours of watching pass without one. baseSketchesPerHour is a first guess — tune so the first insect plate completes inside the MVP playtest. `skill` is the craft the watching trains — Observation in the design doc (§5), `entomology` in the data — and watchXpPerHour credits it per watcher per site-hour, scaled by the site's dig-speed multiplier. The XP is paid for the WATCHING, not the sketch: sketches are a finite lifetime pool (25 across every plate) that rides the fold in insectSketches while skillXp resets, so a per-sketch award would leave a fully-recorded run unable to level this skill at all — and Brush Screens (entomology 8) unbuyable forever. At 50 a lone watcher clears the level-8 gate in ~19 site-hours, and a second body at a second site halves that (the watch is per-site as of 2026-08-12, so hours only stack by spending another slot), so the screens arrive while there are still plates left to be worth doubling.

tending.$note: burst values are first guesses — tune in Phase 1.

bubbles.$note: windfall bubbles — the active-play reward that replaced tap-to-tend. A worked node floats a bubble up the strip every spawnIntervalSec (at most maxLive adrift at once, each living lifetimeSec); catching one grants rewardRatePerSecond x rewardSeconds of that node's resource straight to camp AND tends the node (burst + Choice window + Rite tend deed). lifetimeSec deliberately exceeds spawnIntervalSec so windfalls BANK — glancing away banks 2-3 to pop in a burst instead of silently losing each one, and maxLive is the real ceiling. The haul is FLAT (2026-07-31): it used to be rewardSeconds of the node's OWN live output, which paid 1-2 units at most nodes — at the time an unstaffed node earned only the wandering warden's share (warden.gatherPerSecond / node count; the wander gather-share retired 2026-08-09, wandering is watch-only now), so the windfall shrank every time a zone opened, and the 2026-07-31 kith.gatherPerSecond cut (to 0.1, since raised to 0.3) took another order of magnitude out of the staffed ones. rewardRatePerSecond is the notional gatherer behind the windfall — a minute of somebody's picking at that node, wherever it lands. It was pinned equal to warden.gatherPerSecond (and a validator rule enforced it) until 2026-08-13, when the warden was rescaled to 0.4 for reasons of their own and the pin would have quietly cut the haul from 30 units to 24. The rate stayed at 0.5 and the pin was deleted: the windfall is its own number now, weighed on its own. Which nodes drift a bubble is no longer earned either (2026-08-06): ANY node the run can reach drifts one, worked or fallow. The staffing gate meant every windfall rose from the two or three posts already drawn on the strip and an unposted camp drifted none at all, when a windfall is the land handing something over rather than a wage. spawnIntervalSec and maxLive still meter it, so the pool widened without the payout rate moving. Note a flat haul does not ride the late-game yield multipliers, so re-check its weight against zone 6-8 income in playtest. Held at 0.5 through the 2026-08-13 warden rescale, which is when the old pin to warden.gatherPerSecond was deleted rather than allowed to drag the haul down to 24 units.

warden.$note: The warden's own base hands at their post — always on, boosted by a live burst. Same units as kith.gatherPerSecond, and since 2026-08-13 it rides the node's whole multiplier stack the way a familiar's hands do (it used to sit outside it, so the warden gathered this flat number for the entire run and fell ~70x behind a familiar by the midgame). Rescaled 0.5 -> 0.4 the same day, with the pony and the Birch Frame Pack 0.5 -> 0.2 each: once the hands scaled, a 0.5 base under a +160% band swept the warden from 1.67x a familiar bare to 4.33x fully kitted, and the intended 0.5:0.3 ratio held at one end of the run or the other but never across it. Base and band move together for that reason — retuning either alone re-opens the sweep. Now 1.33x bare, 2.0x kitted, centred near 1.67x. It is the early-game kickstart (assignment, not a tap surge) AND how a bare node earns its first own-resource replant (design §3), so it must stay positive. A bare node has an all-1.0 stack, so this is still exactly the rate the warden picks at virgin ground. It no longer sets the windfall haul: bubbles.rewardRatePerSecond was pinned to this number until the same day and is now tuned on its own.

familiarXp.$note: design §4: familiar run XP + Kinship. famXPToLevel(L) = base·growth^L (60·1.12^L), a powerup choice every 5 levels. xpPerSecond = base run XP a stationed familiar earns per second at its post, a site's watch post included — the watch is work (§2; a watch post gathers nothing as of 2026-08-09 and is one place as of 2026-08-12, and pays the same full rate either way). At Migration run XP converts to Kinship: kinshipGain = floor(√(runXP / kinshipDivisor)); each Kinship level gives +kinshipXpRatePerLevel XP rate and a higher starting level. Levels never scale output. kinshipDivisor tuned to 12000 via the balance model (docs/economy-model.xlsx) — a familiar stationed a whole run banks ~2 Kinship at the first fold; at 1000 it banked ~7. signatureMilestones = the Kinship levels where a familiar's signature deepens (§4's milestone lever): its species trait sharpens by signatureDeepening per milestone (trait value × (1 + 0.25·passed)) and its plate takes an inscription line (§7, species.json). At ~2 Kinship per well-worked fold: first signature around fold 1–2, second around fold 3, third deep in the seasons — first guesses, tune with the fold pacing. The rest are first guesses; postMatch/comfort multipliers (§8) are a later refinement (todo.md).

replant.$note: design §3: replanting a node's own resource raises its richness — the fourth output lane. replantCost(L) = baseCost·growth^L units of the node's OWN resource, spent from camp stock, per node per run; each level adds richnessPerLevel to the node's base yield (richnessMult = 1 + richnessPerLevel·level). No Renown — it pays back in yield, not the ledger. The warden's post trickle self-funds a virgin node's first replant (§3). Richness resets at Migration (except the Almanac's First Planting — a later slice). All first guesses.
